Given: The user is in an existing Chat with the connector-account-access feature enabled and 20 connected connectors available.
When: They open the Connectors panel, close it, and reopen it.
Then: All 20 connectors appear both times. The overview is fetched once, no target refresh is fetched, and the legacy connector and thread endpoints are not read.
finding: An existing Chromium Chat rendered every one of 20 distinct connected accounts on the first and second openings. From before navigation through closing the reopened panel, browser dispatch and loopback ingress both saw one full overview for that chat, no target refresh and no reads of the four legacy endpoints. After the measured interval ended, five separately labelled calibration requests all reached the detector and returned 404. The enabled account-access path became unconditional in #48841.
nextEntry: Reopen if inventory fetching or the account directory changes.

Given: The connector directory contains a saved GitHub account and a saved Acme Search account, and both default accounts require reconnection.
When: The user opens the connector directory, searches for GitHub, then switches to Custom connectors.
Then: GitHub details and Acme Search remain available. No account values are requested, authorization is not updated, and no manual connection is started.
finding: Both saved default accounts required repair. GitHub details remained available in search and Acme Search remained actionable in Custom. Through that point the receiver saw no account-values submission, agent-authorization update or manual grant. A subsequent configuration action exposed the secret input. The frozen values detector watched PUT /api/custom-connectors/:id/values. The agent grant PUT was removed by #49268.
nextEntry: Regress both directories when a credential or connection flow changes.

Given: An admin opens the connector step for a connector with two browser authentication methods.
When: They select that connector from the picker.
Then: A connect dialog named “Choice connector” offers “Workspace OAuth,” and the connector's full catalog entry is read once upon selection.
finding: The admin selected Choice connector from the picker. The detail endpoint had no ingress before selection and one GET after selection. Workspace OAuth was absent while the response was held. Both Workspace OAuth and Personal OAuth were visible in the named dialog after release.
nextEntry: Regress when picker prefetch or connector authentication changes.

Given: An owner opens sharing for a private artifact.
When: The owner selects Organization, Public access, then Only me, copying the link after each change.
Then: Each selected access level becomes checked, and the API receives the changes in that order: organization, public, private. Each copy writes the same canonical app link; there is no text box or copied-link notice before copying, and only one permission-status read occurs.
finding: The private file owner selected organization, public, then private. In each arm the receiver saw one status POST followed by three PUTs carrying those audiences in order. Every selected option became checked and each clipboard write contained the same canonical owner URL. There was no link textbox or copied notice before copying. With invitations disabled the original labels include Only me. With invitations enabled #50474 supplies Workspace, Anyone and Invited people plus a people combobox. Both variants completed the copy sequence.
nextEntry: Regress the classic and invitation-enabled file menus together.

Given: A restored draft contains one annotation mark but no annotated copy.
When: The chat loads and rebuilds the marked-up copy from the original image.
Then: The composer shows one mark and sending becomes enabled; the original image is read once.
finding: The restored draft had one annotation and no annotated copy. The image receiver held its original PNG while the composer showed the mark and disabled Send. One GET returned the PNG. The restored marked draft then enabled Send and still displayed one mark.
nextEntry: Regress when original image loading or draft recovery changes.

Given: A signed-out user opens the sign-in page.
When: The page loads.
Then: The sign-in page remains at /sign-in, and no private conversation snapshot, events, indicators, or agent-list requests are made.
finding: A cold unauthenticated Router visit remained on /sign-in through startup and displayed Clerk. No private snapshot, event, indicator or agent-list dispatch or ingress was observed. The authenticated control displayed its private chat and reached the snapshot receiver. #49933 removed the product GET /api/agents endpoint.
nextEntry: Regress at the signed-out Router boundary on a startup or identity change.

Given: A user is composing a new conversation and the server has not confirmed its creation.
When: They send “Start the local conversation.”
Then: A single “New chat” appears in the sidebar with the requested thread ID before confirmation. No draft is requested.
finding: Sent the frozen text on Home and held thread creation at the receiver. The sidebar displayed exactly one New chat linked to the submitted client thread ID. Through that observation no per-thread draft read was dispatched or received. A confirmed-thread control reached the same draft contract and restored its distinctive text.
nextEntry: Regress when optimistic navigation or draft resolution changes.

Given: A user is composing a new conversation and attaches a QuickTime video named recording.mov; thread creation remains unconfirmed.
When: They send the message with the attachment.
Then: A preview for recording.mov appears using the video URL with a start time of 0.001 seconds. The missing-thread artifact response produces no visible error toast, and creation remains unconfirmed.
finding: With recording.mov attached, the actual send reached an unconfirmed creation and displayed the resolved QuickTime URL ending in #t=0.001 without an error toast. Neither dispatch nor ingress saw a thread-artifacts GET before creation release. An independent confirmed-document control reached that endpoint and received the configured 404. The pending movie page has no 404 to process in this operation.
nextEntry: Keep the original ID open until the pending movie itself triggers a distinguishable missing-thread response, or a sourced upstream decision disposes of that clause.

Given: A user is composing a new conversation with GPT 5.6 Luna selected, and server creation is pending.
When: They change the model to Claude Sonnet 5 and send their first message.
Then: The creation request uses Claude Sonnet 5, the composer still shows Claude Sonnet 5, no draft is requested, and creation remains unconfirmed.
finding: Started with GPT 5.6 Luna, selected Claude Sonnet 5, and sent the first message. While its creation response was held, the request named claude-sonnet-5, the composer showed Claude Sonnet 5, and its pending sidebar entry pointed to the submitted thread. No per-thread draft GET reached the receiver. The confirmed-thread control did retrieve that draft.
nextEntry: Regress pending creation after model preference changes.

Given: An owner opens the ready step with Gmail connected and a chat service available.
When: They start their first task.
Then: Onboarding completes exactly once from the ready step before the first request runs.
finding: The owner opened Ready with Gmail connected. Starting the task produced one onboarding completion POST from /onboarding/ready. Its successful reply preceded the first thread creation and the chat event carrying the ready-step task. The receiver recorded arrivals before interpreting the completion body.
nextEntry: Regress the owner’s Ready handoff.

Given: An invited member needs their own onboarding, cannot add Slack, and has no connected Gmail source.
When: They choose Marketing & content, skip sources, choose to start with Okou, pass Slack with Not now, edit the ready-step request to “Draft my meeting agenda,” and start the task.
Then: The ready step initially shows the asserted competitor-research preset. The first request runs with the edited text, completion is sent once from the ready step, and the member leaves onboarding for chat.
finding: The invited member lacked Gmail and Slack-install permission. They selected Marketing & content, skipped sources, chose Start with Okou, passed Slack with Not now, verified the complete competitor-research preset, and edited it to Draft my meeting agenda. One completion arrived from Ready, before chat creation and dispatch. The resulting chat showed the edited task.
nextEntry: Regress invitation onboarding independently of the owner route.

Given: A new user who needs onboarding opens with the prompt “Draft the launch plan.”
When: They edit it to “Draft the launch plan for the EU market” and choose Next.
Then: Onboarding completes once from the onboarding page before the first chat request runs, and the request uses the edited text with the document and artifact-link instructions appended.
finding: Opened /onboarding with Draft the launch plan, changed it to Draft the launch plan for the EU market and selected Next. One completion arrived from /onboarding. Its reply preceded thread creation and the chat event. The routed chat displayed the edited prompt plus the full document and working artifact-link instructions.
nextEntry: Regress the prompt link and its document instructions.

Given: A signed-in user needs onboarding.
When: The user opens the onboarding page while Marketing records the event request but delays its response.
Then: The industry question appears without waiting for the response. One authenticated POST is sent to https://www.okou.ai/api/events with the onboarding-start tag and a UUID event ID; one started telemetry record for the user and organization exists before the POST, with no status code, and the request remains un-aborted.
finding: One started record for the fixture user and organization, tagged onboarding-start and without a status code, crossed the analytics SDK boundary before dispatch. The Marketing receiver got one authenticated POST to https://www.okou.ai/api/events with a UUID. While the response was held the industry question was interactive, the selected radio changed and the associated request signal remained live.
nextEntry: Regress the authenticated Marketing and analytics boundaries together.

Given: The Discord approval callback has a valid proof and an open opener.
When: The callback page starts approval and the opener closes immediately afterward.
Then: It reports that authorization was interrupted or refreshed, does not show an Open Discord link, submits exactly one approval request, and removes the proof from the URL.
finding: A native Chromium callback opened from a real window with a fresh proof issued by the local API. The full browser context and HTTP relay each observed one approval POST. PostgreSQL-backed approval returned 200 while the opener was alive. Closing it before delivering that response left the interrupted notice, no Open Discord link and no URL proof. A second isolated arm again observed one page attempt. The separate relay replay produced an extra 400 after the accepted 200.
nextEntry: Regress the native callback with the arrival journal and the rejected replay control.

Given: A suggestion's custom-direction dialog contains a typed follow-up, and sending it initially fails.
When: The user retries the send and the server accepts it.
Then: The failure leaves the dialog and its text intact; the retry uses the same chat and event identities and includes the suggestion background and follow-up. Acceptance closes the dialog, removes the card, shows the sent confirmation and All caught up, and leaves the user on For you; no ordinary card-consumption request is recorded.
finding: The inline editor retained the suggestion and typed follow-up after failure and reused the chat and event IDs on retry. The isolated product API recorded 409 then 201 and persisted the background and follow-up with that same event. The card and editor disappeared. The sent confirmation and All caught up appeared on /for-you. No page request reached the ordinary consume endpoint before or after the successful retry. The inspection control alone performed the rejected ordinary consume. #49016 replaced the dialog with the inline surface.
nextEntry: Regress the inline retry and its ordinary-consume boundary.

Given: The user opens Debug and the Morning Brief action is enabled.
When: The user focuses the action and presses Enter.
Then: The brief completes, and exactly one request is submitted.
finding: Focused the enabled Morning Brief action and pressed Enter. The receiver had no brief request before Enter and one POST through the final chat-link readback. The page stayed busy while held and showed completion plus the correct chat link after release.
nextEntry: Regress keyboard activation when the Debug action changes.

Given: A connected member sees an Everyday card and a recent purchase in Link activity.
When: They return to the tab and focus it, then the workspace wallet changes to a Business card and updated purchase.
Then: Returning to the tab preserves the existing card and transaction without extra requests. During refresh the old data remains visible; after refresh, Business is marked default and replaces Everyday, and the updated purchase replaces the recent purchase.
finding: With Everyday and Recent purchase visible, hid the wallet tab, returned and focused it. No wallet status, card or activity read was dispatched or received before publication, including an independent local socket round trip. A workspace wallet notification then reached all three endpoints. In separate delivery orders, the unchanged section stayed visible until its own reply. Business became default, Updated purchase appeared, and both old values disappeared.
nextEntry: Regress focus and workspace notification independently in both delivery orders.

Given: I have reviewed a host-creation draft containing password old-pass, and token acquisition is pending when I save.
When: The signed-in owner changes before the old owner's token resolves.
Then: The draft closes, the secret is cleared, and no host creation request is sent.
finding: The reviewed VNC draft used the old owner's fixture password. Saving waited on that owner's credential. After identity changed the draft closed, and the new owner's login field was empty. No create reached the receiver with the old credential either released or held. As a control, releasing the original owner's credential without switching produced a 201 host creation.
nextEntry: Regress both old-credential delivery orders on an identity change.

Given: A remote browser viewer is open with FPS hidden.
When: The user opens Browser settings and chooses FPS > On from the left-opening radio submenu, then chooses Off and reopens the submenu.
Then: Off is initially selected, and On displays a 128-by-48 FPS overlay without sending browser requests. On and Off selections are reflected when the submenu is reopened; Off removes the overlay, and Escape returns focus to Browser settings.
finding: After the streaming viewer acknowledged a control text input over the local CDP socket, FPS was hidden. Off started checked in the left-opening submenu. On showed the 128 by 48 overlay, On was checked on reopening, Off removed it, and Escape restored Browser settings focus. Neither the sender nor the independent WebSocket peer observed a protocol command between the preflight receipt and the completed menu sequence. The earlier startup-only observation could include a late Runtime.evaluate. The acknowledged-input preflight separates that initialization.
nextEntry: Regress on the existing receiver after streaming initialization has completed.

Given: A multipart recording upload's storage transfer succeeds, but the completion request returns a 404 with the message Multipart upload not found.
When: The user uploads the recording.
Then: That finalization message is shown once; completion is requested once, and no generic upload-failure message appears.
finding: Five numbered storage PUTs succeeded before one multipart completion POST returned 404. While that response was held there was no completion error. On delivery the page displayed Multipart upload not found once, retained the typed draft, and displayed no generic upload-failed message.
nextEntry: Regress the storage and finalization boundaries together.
